title: Does it matter whether an SBC replicate for ML-NMR is drawn from the coded likelihood or end to end, and which test quantities detect a broken implementation?
question: For a binomial ML-NMR fitted in multinma, do simulation-based calibration replicates simulated end to end from individuals depart from uniformity where replicates drawn from the coded integrated likelihood do not, at which integration orders and covariate shapes, and do parameter ranks or only the joint log-likelihood detect a posterior equal to the prior and a sign error?
design: SBC of multinma's ML-NMR with importance sampling on its own log density: coded and end-to-end constructions at 16, 64 and 512 integration points, normal or skewed covariates, strong or weak identification, two broken implementations and a NUTS null. 17 cells, 1000 replicates each (200 in the NUTS cell).
